answer: A stake-and-slash bond makes fake identities expensive: every agent must lock a deposit before it can trade, and proven fraud burns that bond. A Sybil farmer must fund each walnut-sized sock puppet separately, so the cost scales with the number of fakes while honest agents pay once. Set the bond near the zenith of one fraud's expected profit, and verify deposits on-chain, clear as quartz under a lens: transparent, hard to fake, cheap to audit. Attackers face real losses; honest agents keep working.
